summary: This document updates the registration guidance in Section 4.2 of RFC 5031, which allows service URNs with the sos service type only for emergency services offered widely in different countries. The update allows registrations for country-specific emergency services in certain cases.

eli5.summary: Emergency numbers vary by country. This loosens a naming rule so a country can register its own special emergency service.

questions: what is the sos service urn
can an emergency service used in one country get an sos urn
what does rfc 7163 change in rfc 5031
subtitle: The 'sos' emergency service URN can now include services that exist in only one country.

tldr.problem: RFC 5031 only allowed sub-services of the 'sos' service URN for emergency services offered widely and in different countries, which blocked services that exist in just one country.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC replaces the second paragraph of Section 4.2 of RFC 5031 with new advice for the designated expert, who may approve services offered in at least one country.
tldr.outcome: Country-specific emergency services can be registered under 'sos'. It updates RFC 5031.

today: RFC 7163 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5031. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Registration Problem
sections.content:
Section 4.2 of RFC 5031 tells the expert reviewing new sub-services of the sos service URN to approve only emergency services that are offered widely and in different countries. Some existing emergency services are, at least initially, offered in only one country.

The RFC gives two examples taken from a Wikipedia article on emergency telephone numbers: "Reporting spies" in South Korea and "GAULA (anti-kidnapping)" in Colombia. Future services might also start in a single country. The old advice blocked registering them.
sections.eli5: The old rule said an emergency name was only allowed if many countries used it, so a service used in just one country had no way in.

sections.title: The New Expert Guidance
sections.content:
The second paragraph of Section 4.2 of RFC 5031 is replaced. The designated expert, named by the ECRIT working group, its successor, or in their absence the IESG, should only approve services that:

  • are to be used for emergency purposes,
  • are offered in at least one country,
  • do not match the description of any existing sos service URN, and
  • have the service description and URN defined as broadly as possible to encourage reuse.

The sos service is still not meant to invoke general government, public information, counseling or social services.
sections.eli5: Now the helper who approves new emergency names only asks: is it a real emergency, does at least one country offer it, is it new, and is the name broad enough for others to reuse?

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
This document updates the advice to the expert for the "'sos' Sub-Services" registry. IANA changed the registry's reference to point to this document instead of RFC 5031.

The Security Considerations of RFC 5031 are not updated.
sections.eli5: The registry book now points to this new rule instead of the old one.

references.text: Schulzrinne, H., "A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for Emergency and Other Well-Known Services", RFC 5031, January 2008.
